title: A Clean Slate
summary: The PC's Security log is almost empty: someone cleared it. Luckily a copy of every event was also sent to your box as it happened. Rebuild what they hid and undo it.
story: {{CO}} (made up) has a design PC, {{PC}}, on 10.10.28.0/24. Its Security log says only one thing: it was cleared. Your box, soc, keeps a forwarded copy of that log in /var/log/forwarded. You also have the PC's administrator password: {{ADMPW}} (winrm-shell -i 10.10.28.30 -u Administrator -p {{ADMPW}}).
goal: Find who cleared the log and how, where they signed in from and the account they made; capture the flag in their pickup folder; then delete that account and the start-up file they left before the next sign-in copies the plans out.
skills: event 1102 (log cleared), why logs are forwarded, the Startup folder, Remove-LocalUser, Remove-Item

events.message: The audit log was cleared. Subject: Account Name: {{VIC}}

flags.name: The flag in the pickup folder

questions.ask: Which account cleared the Security log?
questions.explain: Event 1102 on the PC names it, and the forwarded copy agrees.

questions.ask: Which program did they use to clear it (wevtutil or powershell)?
questions.explain: The 4688 (new process) line just before the 1102 in the forwarded copy: {{CLEARCMD}}.

questions.ask: From what address did that account sign in?

questions.explain: The forwarded 4720 and 4732 lines: created and added to Administrators.

tasks.name: Remove the file they put in the Startup folder
tasks.explain: Remove-Item on the file in C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp

attacker.note: Someone signed in, the start-up file ran and copied the plans share into the public pickup folder.

hints.text: Clearing a log is itself logged (event 1102), so the clearing account is easy. Everything before it is gone from the PC - but not from your box: cat /var/log/forwarded/*.log on soc is a copy made as the events happened.

The forwarded copy shows the remote sign-in, the account made and the program that cleared the log. Things that run at every sign-in can sit in C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp. Remove that file and the account (Remove-LocalUser).
